goals: Provide a reliable 1:1 counseling booking system with persistence.
Ensure atomic booking operations to prevent double-booking.
Implement a secure lookup and cancellation mechanism based on email verification.
Maintain a clean separation between domain logic and storage.
user_flows: Counselor adds a slot -> Client queries slots -> Client books slot -> Booking confirmed.
Client provides booking ID and email -> System verifies and returns booking details.
Client provides booking ID and email -> System verifies -> Booking cancelled -> Slot becomes available again.

domain_entities.name: Slot
domain_entities.description: A specific time window offered by a counselor.

domain_entities.name: Booking
domain_entities.description: A reservation made by a client for a specific slot.

business_rules: A slot can only be booked if its current state is 'Available'.
Booking creation must be atomic: marking the slot as booked and creating the booking record must happen in one transaction.
A booking can only be looked up or cancelled if the provided email matches the email stored in the booking record.
Cancelling a booking must automatically set the associated slot's state back to 'Available'.
Booking IDs must be unique UUIDs.
edge_cases: Two clients attempting to book the same slot simultaneously (Race condition).
Client attempting to cancel a booking that is already cancelled.
Client attempting to lookup a booking with a valid ID but incorrect email.
Counselor adding a slot that already exists for the same time and counselor.
Invalid ISO 8601 date formats provided in requests.
design_decisions: Use SQLite for lightweight, file-based persistence.
Use ISO 8601 strings for date-time storage to ensure timezone consistency (Asia/Seoul).
Implement a custom Exception hierarchy for domain-specific errors (e.g., SlotAlreadyBookedError).
Use a Service Layer pattern (`CounselingService`) to encapsulate all business logic.
assumptions: All counseling slots are exactly 30 minutes long.
The system does not need to handle counselor schedules/conflicts beyond the existence of a slot.
Email is used as the primary verification token for clients.

data_models.Slot: dataclass(id: int, counselor_id: str, start_time: str, is_booked: bool)
data_models.Booking: dataclass(booking_id: str, slot_id: int, client_name: str, client_email: str, status: str)

methods.name: add_available_slot
methods.signature: add_available_slot(self, counselor_id: str, start_time: str) -> None

methods.name: query_available_slots
methods.signature: query_available_slots(self, counselor_id: Optional[str] = None, date: Optional[str] = None) -> List[Slot]
methods.notes: date filter should match 'YYYY-MM-DD' part of start_time

methods.name: create_booking
methods.signature: create_booking(self, counselor_id: str, start_time: str, client_name: str, client_email: str) -> str

methods.name: lookup_booking
methods.signature: lookup_booking(self, booking_id: str, client_email: str) -> Booking

methods.name: cancel_booking
methods.signature: cancel_booking(self, booking_id: str, client_email: str) -> None

database_ddl: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS slots (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, counselor_id TEXT NOT NULL, start_time TEXT NOT NULL, is_booked INTEGER DEFAULT 0)

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bookings (booking_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, slot_id INTEGER NOT NULL, client_name TEXT NOT NULL, client_email TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY(slot_id) REFERENCES slots(id))
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_slots_counselor_time ON slots(counselor_id, start_time)
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bookings_email ON bookings(client_email)
